title: A Model-based Visual Contact Localization and Force Sensing System for Compliant Robotic Grippers
summary: Grasp force estimation can help prevent robots from damaging delicate objects during manipulation and improve learning-based robotic control. Integrating force sensing into deformable grippers negotiates trade-offs in cost, complexity, mechanical robustness, and performance. With the growing integration of RGB-D wrist cameras into robotic systems for control purposes, camera-based techniques are a promising solution for indirect visual force estimation. Current approaches mostly utilize end-to-end deep learning, which can be brittle when generalizing to new scenarios, while existing model-based approaches are unsuited to grasping and modern grasper geometries. To address these challenges, we developed a model-based visual force sensing approach integrating an iterative contact localization with generalization to unseen objects. The system extracts structural key points from wrist camera RGB-D images of deforming fin-ray-shaped soft grippers, and uses these key points to define parameters of an inverse finite element analysis simulation in Simulation Open Framework Architecture. The iterative contact localization sub-system utilizes a deep learning-based online 3D reconstruction and pose estimation pipeline to dynamically update contact location, and is robust to visual occlusion and unseen objects. Our system demonstrated an average root mean square error of 0.23 N and normalized root mean square deviation of 2.11% during the load phase, and 0.48 N and 4.34% over the entire grasping process when interacting with different objects under various conditions, showcasing its potential for real-time model-based indirect force sensing of soft grippers.
tldr: The paper introduces a model‑based visual force‑sensing system for compliant robotic grippers that uses key points extracted from wrist‑camera RGB‑D images to drive an inverse FEM simulation, achieving low force estimation error across varied objects.
tldr_zh: 该论文提出了一种基于模型的视觉力传感方法，利用腕部相机获取的RGB‑D图像关键点驱动逆有限元分析，从而实现对柔性夹爪的接触定位与力估计，并在多种物体上取得了较高的测量精度。
summary_zh:
摘要：
抓取力估计可以帮助防止机器人在操作过程中损坏精细物体，并改进基于学习的机器人控制。将力传感集成到可变形夹爪中可以权衡成本、复杂度、机械鲁棒性和性能。随着RGB-D腕部相机越来越多地集成到用于控制的机器人系统中，基于相机的技术是间接视觉力估计的一种有前景的解决方案。当前的方法主要使用端到端深度学习，这在泛化到新场景时可能很脆弱，而现有的基于模型的方法不适用于抓取和现代夹爪几何形状。为了应对这些挑战，我们开发了一种基于模型的视觉力感知方法，将迭代接触定位与对未见过物体的泛化相结合。该系统从变形鳍射线形软夹爪的腕部相机RGB-D图像中提取结构关键点，并使用这些关键点来定义Simulation Open Framework Architecture中逆有限元分析仿真的参数。迭代接触定位子系统利用基于深度学习的在线三维重建和位姿估计管道来动态更新接触位置，并对视觉遮挡和未见过物体具有鲁棒性。我们的系统在加载阶段的平均均方根误差为0.23 N，归一化均方根偏差为2.11%，在整个抓取过程中为0.48 N和4.34%，在不同条件下与不同物体交互时表现出色，展示了其用于软夹爪实时基于模型的间接力传感的潜力。

title: Multi-frame Restoration for High-rate Lissajous Confocal Laser Endomicroscopy
summary: Lissajous confocal laser endomicroscopy (CLE) is a promising solution for high speed in vivo optical biopsy for handheld scenarios. However, Lissajous scanning traces a resonant trajectory and samples only the visited pixels per frame; at high frame rates, many pixels remain unvisited, creating structured holes. In this work, we introduce the first benchmark for high-rate Lissajous CLE, consisting of low-quality video clips paired with high-quality reference images. The reference images are wide-FOV mosaics obtained by stitching stabilized, slow-scan frames of the same tissue, enabling temporally aligned supervision. Using this dataset, we propose MIRA, a lightweight recurrent framework for Lissajous CLE restoration that iteratively aggregates temporal context through feature reuse and displacement alignment. Our experiments demonstrate that MIRA outperforms both lightweight and high-complexity baselines in restoration quality while maintaining a favorable computational efficiency suitable for clinical deployment.
tldr: A new benchmark dataset and a lightweight recurrent network (MIRA) to restore high-rate Lissajous confocal laser endomicroscopy images by aggregating temporal context.
tldr_zh: 提出首个高帧率Lissajous共聚焦激光内窥镜成像的基准数据集，并设计轻量级循环网络MIRA，通过时间上下文聚合实现图像修复。
summary_zh: Lissajous共聚焦激光内镜显微镜(CLE)是一种有望实现手持场景下高速活体光学活检的解决方案。然而，Lissajous扫描呈现共振轨迹，每帧仅对访问过的像素进行采样；在高帧率下，许多像素未被访问，形成结构化缺失。本研究提出了首个高帧率Lissajous CLE基准数据集，由低质量视频片段与高质量参考图像配对组成。参考图像为通过对同一组织进行稳定慢速扫描并拼接而获得的宽视野马赛克图像，实现了时间对齐的监督。利用该数据集，本研究提出了MIRA——一个用于Lissajous CLE图像重建的轻量级循环框架，通过特征复用和位移对齐迭代聚合时间上下文信息。实验表明，MIRA在重建质量上优于轻量级和高复杂度基线方法，同时保持适合临床部署的计算效率。
